newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond trade ideas - Buy EIB in lira.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond trade ideas - Buy EIB in lira.

text.p: Eurobond analysts' latest trade recommendations focused on Eurodollars, lira, sterling and yen.

In the buoyant lira sector, San Paolo recommended buying EIB bonds which have outperformed other paper. In dollars, Credit Lyonnais recommended buying Ontario bonds as Canadian spreads continued to tighten on positive credit ratings outlook.
Following are latest trade ideas, compiled by Reuters:
STRATEGY There has been a general tightening of spreads
of both provincial and federal Canadian paper. This is largely due to a positive ratings outlook. This bond is at around 13 b.p. and there is potential for further spread tightening.
STRATEGY This credit improving, duration neutral trade
can currently be done for a yield pick-up of 25 b.p. The trade is cash neutral.
STRATEGY Retail buying has driven the spread on the

British Gas bond in sharply over the past few months and good switches can now be found both up and down the curve. Going longer it can be switched into JR East for a five b.p. pickup and a four notch credit pickup. Going shorter it can be switched into Ford to pick up three b.p. and two notches of credit.
STRATEGY This trade can be done for even yield for a
four notch upgrade in credit from A2 to Aa1. The trade also takes out two points in cash.
STRATEGY Over the last month EIB has outperformed Helaba

by approximately 25 b.p. in price terms. EIB is expensive against the swap and the BTP (trading respectively at around 29 b.p. and 30 b.p. through). Helaba is cheap against the swap and the BTP (trading respectively at around 12 and 13 b.p. through) and offers a 16 b.p. pick up in yield.
STRATEGY This allows a shorter duration while picking up

about 22 b.p. in yield. Also, the EIB 7.55 percent is expensive against the swap and the BTP (trading respectively at around 47 b.p. and 25 b.p. through). Over the last month EIB 9.60 pct has underperformed EIB 7.55 percent by approximately 35 b.p. in price terms. EIB 9.60 pct is cheap against the swap, at around 14 b.p. through.
STRATEGY Over the last month KfW has outperformed EIB by

around 60 b.p. in price terms. KfW is expensive against the swap and the BTP (trading respectively at around 35 b.p. and 32 b.p. through). This switch allows shorter duration while gaining around an 11 b.p. pick up in yield.
STRATEGY Over the last month World Bank has outperformed

Eurofima by approximately 70 b.p. in price terms. Eurofima is cheap for a supranational, trading at around 10 b.p. through the swap and around 20 b.p. through the BTP. This switch gives shorter duration for a 21 b.p. yield pick-up.
STRATEGY This bond is cheap against the swap, trading at
around six b.p. through and cheap against the BTP, trading at around 15 b.p. through. It also trades on a bid/offer spread of around 25 b.p.
STRATEGY This trade gives a yield give-up of around 121
basis points. Due to the Eurosterling curve flattening the spread between the two bonds listed above has widened by around 80 b.p.
STRATEGY The Euroyen market has seen a slight tightening

of spreads over the last week. This could lead to selling and some modest widening. Some 10-year issues still look cheap relative to shorter-dated bonds, providing an incentive to switch longer. The trade fits into the general expectation of curve flattening in the near term.
